story: You are a researcher at the Bureau of Labor Statistics conducting a comprehensive study on labor market dynamics and policy impacts. You are collecting detailed data from a longitudinal survey of workers across various industries to understand how different employment statuses, education levels, and policy implementations affect job satisfaction, income, and overall well-being.

variables.name: AnnualIncomeBracket
variables.desc: income range in thousands of dollars

variables.name: CommuteTimeCategory
variables.desc: commute time to work in minutes

variables.name: TrainingAndDevelopmentOpportunities
variables.desc: availability of training and development opportunities

questions.question: List all variables that 'EmploymentType' has a causal effect on.
Does knowing the value of 'JobSatisfactionLevel' change the probability distribution of 'HealthcarePlanType'?
Conditioning on 'OvertimeEligibility', is 'TeleworkOption' statistically independent of 'WorkplaceSafetyRating'?
Does knowing the value of 'EmploymentStatus' change the probability distribution of 'CommuteTimeCategory', even after accounting for 'RetirementPlanOption'?
